mainTopic: Can lift-items be acquired by משיכה? Then רב and שמואל on when a buyer acquires grain sold by measure, defended against a ברייתא.
overview: The גמרא asks whether something normally lifted can also be acquired by pulling (משיכה). It first brings our משנה about produce acquired by pulling. It answers that the משנה means huge bundles that are dragged, not carried. The flax case in the סיפא challenges this answer, and the גמרא explains that flax slips apart, so it is only made into small bundles that are lifted. רבינא then brings a משנה where the חכמים say small animals are acquired by משיכה. רב אשי answers that animals cling to the ground, so pulling is their normal way of moving. Next, רב and שמואל teach that if a seller sells a whole כור as one unit, he can back out until the last סאה is measured. If he sets a price per סאה, each סאה becomes the buyer's as it is measured. A ברייתא seems to say each portion is acquired before the vessel is full, and the גמרא answers that the case was priced per לוג in a vessel with marking lines. The amud ends as the גמרא begins a new challenge about hiring a worker, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from produce acquired by pulling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the משנה that produce is acquired by משיכה, even though produce is normally lifted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: if someone sells produce and the buyer pulled it but did not measure it, the buyer acquires it. But produce is normally lifted, and still the משנה says it is acquired by pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to show that something normally lifted can be acquired by pulling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual rule is that each item is acquired the normal way it is moved. Produce can be picked up, so you would expect it to need הגבהה. Yet the משנה says משיכה is enough, which challenges the view that lift-items need lifting.

keyTerms.meaning: Pulling the item toward oneself, a way of acquiring
Lifting the item, a way of acquiring

phrases.english: Come and hear: one who sells produce to his fellow,
if he pulled but did not measure, he acquires.
But produce is something that is normally lifted,
and yet it teaches that he acquires by pulling!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this section by testing the question of whether lift-items can be acquired by משיכה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that items normally lifted cannot be acquired by משיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Produce is a lift-item, yet the משנה says משיכה acquires it.

steps.title: The produce is in huge bundles
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the משנה is talking about bundles too big to lift, so pulling is their normal way of moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Large bundles.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes off the proof by limiting the משנה to large bundles of produce.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Huge bundles are not carried; they are dragged. For them, משיכה is the normal way of moving, so the משנה proves nothing about items that really are normally lifted.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here?

phrases.english: What are we dealing with here?
With large bundles.
phrases.notes: Bundles so big that people drag them instead of carrying them.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the משנה to a special case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed ordinary produce, but the case may be bundles too big to lift.

steps.title: Challenge from the flax case
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה means big bundles, why does the סיפא say flax needs lifting? Flax also comes in big bundles.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: one who buys flax does not acquire it until he moves it from one place to another. Don't people make flax into big bundles too?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 2 using the next part of the same משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first case was about big bundles, the flax case should be about big bundles too. Big bundles can be acquired by pulling, yet the משנה requires flax to be carried. So the 'big bundles' answer looks wrong.

phrases.english: If so, say the end clause:
one who buys flax from his fellow
has not acquired it until he carries it
from this place to another place.

phrases.aramaic: אַטּוּ פִּשְׁתָּן בִּשְׁלִיפֵי רַבְרְבֵי מִי לָא עָבְדִי?!
phrases.english: Is it so that flax is not made into large bundles?!

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the משנה deals with large bundles.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flax also comes in big bundles, yet the משנה requires carrying it, so 'big bundles' cannot explain the difference.

steps.title: Flax slips apart
steps.stepSummary: Flax is different: big bundles of it slip apart, so it is packed in small bundles that are lifted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Flax is different, because it slips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the big-bundles answer by explaining why flax is an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Flax slides out of large bundles, so people don't make big flax bundles. Small bundles are carried, so flax needs הגבהה. The big-bundles reading of the first case stays in place.

phrases.english: Flax is different, because it slips.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case (flax is an exception)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flax could also be made into big bundles and dragged.
steps.terutzMaskana: Flax slips, so it is only made into small bundles that are lifted.
steps.whatToRemember: The produce proof fails: the משנה speaks of big bundles that are dragged, and flax needs lifting because it is only made into small bundles.

steps.title: רבינא brings proof from small animals
steps.stepSummary: רבינא cites a משנה where חכמים say small animals are acquired by משיכה, even though small animals can be lifted.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Come and hear: a large animal is acquired by handing over, and a small one by lifting, says רבי מאיר and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר. The חכמים say a small animal is acquired by pulling. But a small animal can be lifted, and still it is acquired by pulling!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא brings a new source to show that something that can be lifted is acquired by משיכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small animal like a sheep can be picked up, so you would expect it to need הגבהה. Yet the חכמים say משיכה works, which seems to prove that lift-items can be acquired by pulling.

keyTerms.meaning: A large domestic animal (like a cow)
A small domestic animal (like a sheep)
Handing over the reins, a way of acquiring

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע:
phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi: Come and hear:
a large animal is acquired by handing over,
and the small one by lifting;

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר.
phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.
And the Sages say: a small animal is acquired by pulling.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא בְּהֵמָה דַּקָּה, דְּבַר הַגְבָּהָה הִיא,
phrases.english: But a small animal is something that can be lifted,
and yet it teaches that one acquires it by pulling!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי, תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the produce proof failed, a new source is brought for the same question.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that lift-items cannot be acquired by משיכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A small animal can be lifted, yet the חכמים allow משיכה.

steps.title: Animals cling to the ground
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that animals are different because they resist being lifted, so pulling is their normal way of moving.
steps.simpleTranslation: Animals are different, because they cling.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי pushes off רבינא's proof by explaining that animals are a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An animal digs in and resists when you try to pick it up, so the normal way to move it is to lead or pull it. That is why משיכה works for small animals, which tells us nothing about other lift-items.

phrases.english: An animal is different, because it clings.
phrases.notes: It holds onto the ground and is hard to pick up, so people pull it instead.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Limits the proof to animals only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Animals are normally moved by pulling, so they are not true lift-items.
steps.whatToRemember: Both proofs fail for the same reason: in each case pulling was really the normal way to move that item (big bundles, clinging animals).

steps.title: Selling a whole כור as one unit
steps.stepSummary: רב and שמואל rule that if the seller sold a כור for thirty as one deal, he can back out even before the last סאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב and שמואל both say: if he said 'I am selling you a כור for thirty,' he can back out, even at the last סאה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new teaching of רב and שמואל about when a sale of measured grain is final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller agreed to sell only a full כור as one unit. Until the full amount is measured, the deal is not complete, so he may still back out even when just one סאה is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: A large measure, equal to thirty סאה
To back out of the deal

phrases.english: Rav and Shmuel both say:
'I am selling you a kor for thirty,'
phrases.notes: Thirty סלעים for a כור, which holds thirty סאה.

phrases.english: he can back out,
even at the last se'a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic about sales by measure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כור sold as one unit is not acquired until fully measured, so the seller may back out until then.

steps.title: Pricing per סאה makes each one final
steps.stepSummary: If the seller priced it per סאה, the buyer acquires each סאה as it is measured.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'I am selling you a כור for thirty, a סאה for a סלע,' each one is acquired as it comes.
steps.whatsHappening: רב and שמואל give the contrasting case: when each סאה is priced on its own, each one becomes the buyer's as it is measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'a סאה for a סלע' turns the deal into many small sales. Each measured סאה is a finished sale, so the seller can stop going forward but cannot undo what was already measured.

keyTerms.meaning: Each one, as it comes, is acquired

phrases.aramaic: ״כּוֹר בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים – סְאָה בְּסֶלַע אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״ –
phrases.english: 'A kor for thirty, a se'a for a sela, I am selling you,'
each first one, he acquires.
phrases.notes: Each סאה becomes the buyer's as soon as it is measured.

steps.triggerLanguage: ״כּוֹר בִּשְׁלֹשִׁים – סְאָה בְּסֶלַע אֲנִי מוֹכֵר לָךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second half of the same teaching, contrasting with step 7.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When priced per סאה, each measured סאה is acquired immediately.
steps.whatToRemember: Whole-unit price: nothing is final until the end. Per-סאה price: each סאה is final as it is measured.
steps.confusionAlert: In both cases the total is thirty for a כור. The only difference is whether the seller also set a price per סאה, and that changes everything.

steps.title: A ברייתא seems to say each portion is acquired before the measure is full
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא: if the measuring vessel belonged to one of the parties, each portion is acquired as it goes in, even though the vessel is not yet full.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If the measuring vessel belonged to one of them, each portion is acquired one after another. That means he acquires even though the measure was not yet filled!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב and שמואל from a ברייתא. The ברייתא seems to say the buyer acquires each bit as it goes in, without waiting for the vessel to fill.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל said that when a כור is sold as one unit, the buyer does not acquire until the whole measure is completed. The ברייתא says without any limit that each portion is acquired as it goes in, even before the vessel is full. Since it does not limit this to a per-unit price, it seems to contradict רב and שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Each portion is acquired as it comes, one after another

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיְתָה מִדָּה שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן –
phrases.english: If the measuring vessel belonged to one of them,
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא quoted earlier on 85a, about whose vessel is used for measuring.

phrases.english: he acquires each portion, one by one.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּלֹא נִתְמַלְּאָה הַמִּדָּה!
phrases.english: And that is even though the measure was not filled!
phrases.notes: These are the גמרא's own words, pointing out the problem. They are not part of the ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: אִם הָיְתָה מִדָּה שֶׁל אֶחָד מֵהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of רב and שמואל that acquisition waits for the full measure.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a buyer does not acquire until the full measure is filled.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has acquisition happening portion by portion, before the vessel is full.

steps.title: The sale was priced per לוג and the vessel had markings
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא is about a seller who priced each לוג separately. Like the markings on the הין described by רב כהנא, these vessels had markings, so each לוג was finished as it was measured.
steps.simpleTranslation: For example, he said to him: 'I am selling you a הין for twelve סלעים, one לוג for each סלע.' And as רב כהנא said, there were markings on the הין. Here too, there were markings on the measuring vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is a case where each לוג had its own price. The vessel had lines marking each לוג, so each לוג counts as a finished measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits step 8: when each unit is priced on its own, the buyer acquires each unit as soon as it is measured. The markings matter because they show exactly when each לוג is full. So the ברייתא does not contradict רב and שמואל. Each לוג really was a complete measure.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure equal to twelve לוג

steps.whatToRemember: A buyer acquires bit by bit only when each bit is priced separately and its measure is clearly completed. That is why the vessel's markings are important.

phrases.english: For example, where he said to him:
"A hin for twelve sela'im,
phrases.notes: A הין holds twelve לוג, so this works out to exactly one סלע per לוג.

phrases.english: one log for a sela, I am selling to you";
and this is like what Rav Kahana said:
There were markings on the hin,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the הין vessel used in the בית המקדש for measuring the drink offerings.

phrases.english: here too,
there were markings on the measuring vessels.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 by narrowing the ברייתא to a specific case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the sale was priced per unit, and the vessel had markings.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא lets the buyer acquire before any full measure is completed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each marked לוג was its own sale, and each one was complete when acquired.

steps.title: A new challenge begins: hiring a worker for harvest at a דינר a day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts to quote a new source about someone who hires a worker for the threshing season at one דינר a day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One who hires a worker to work with him at the threshing floor for one דינר a day...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next challenge. It begins quoting a source about hiring a worker, and the case continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the opening of the case appears here: the worker's job and his daily wage. The challenge itself comes on the next amud, so for now we are just getting the facts in place.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor; here, the harvest season

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who hires a worker
to work with him at the threshing floor
for a dinar a day,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new challenge after step 10 resolved the previous one.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of רב and שמואל about a sale and its price (the full challenge continues on the next amud).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated; the source is still being quoted.
